extName.description: Extension name, shown in the browser's extension list.

extDescription.message: Checks the page you're on with your own PhishNet Detector API (phishnet serve) and shows its phishing risk score.
extDescription.description: Extension description, shown in the browser's extension list.

popupWhy.description: Heading above the list of matched signals.

popupApi.description: Footer label before the API address.

popupNoAddress.message: PhishNet couldn't read this tab's address. Click the toolbar icon while on the page you want to check.

popupUnsupportedPage.message: Only regular web pages (http:// and https://) can be checked.

hintUnreachable.message: Start it with "phishnet serve" (or the Docker image), or set the right address in Settings. A server on another machine needs PhishNet 2.4.0 or newer.

hintTimeout.message: Something is listening at that address but didn't reply. Check that it's a PhishNet API, or try again.

hintAuth.message: Open Settings and paste the API key that "phishnet serve" printed when it first started (it's stored in ~/.phishnet/api-key on the server).

hintRate.message: The server limits how many scans can be made per minute. Wait a moment, then try again.

errInvalidKey.message: The API key can't contain spaces or special characters - copy it exactly as printed.

errEnterAddress.message: Enter the API address, for example $URL$

errInvalidAddress.message: That doesn't look like a valid address.

errProtocol.message: The address must start with http:// or https://

errAddressExtras.message: Use just the server address, without a login, query string, or #fragment.

errTimeout.message: PhishNet API at $URL$ didn't answer within $SECONDS$ seconds.

errUnreachable.message: Can't reach PhishNet API at $URL$ — is "phishnet serve" running?

errKeyRejected.message: PhishNet API rejected the API key.

errKeyRequired.message: PhishNet API requires an API key.

errHttpNotApi.message: $URL$ answered with HTTP $STATUS$, not like a PhishNet API. Check the address in Settings.

errNotApiCheckSettings.message: $URL$ answered, but not like a PhishNet API. Check the address in Settings.

errNotScanResult.message: $URL$ answered, but not with a PhishNet scan result. Check the address in Settings.

errNotApi.message: $URL$ answered, but not like a PhishNet API.

optionsApiAddressHelp.message: Where your `phishnet serve` instance is listening. The default, `http://localhost:8080`, matches `phishnet serve` and the Docker image run with `-p 8080:8080`. For another port or machine, enter e.g. `http://localhost:9090` or `http://192.168.1.20:8080`.
optionsApiAddressHelp.description: Text between backticks is shown as code.

optionsApiKeyPlaceholder.message: paste the key printed by phishnet serve

optionsShow.description: Checkbox that shows the API key in plain text.

optionsApiKeyHelp.message: Since version 2.9.0, `phishnet serve` requires an API key. It prints the key when it first starts and stores it in `~/.phishnet/api-key` on the server; a new one can be made with `phishnet serve --regenerate-key`. Leave this empty for a server started with `--no-auth`. The key is kept in this browser's extension storage.
optionsApiKeyHelp.description: Text between backticks is shown as code.

optionsLanguageHelp.message: Language of the popup and this page. The API is asked to answer in the same language. Takes effect right away.

optionsPrivacyText.message: Pages are only checked when you click the PhishNet toolbar icon. The extension then sends that one page's address to the API address above - your own server - and nowhere else. Nothing runs in the background.

optionsSavedWithKey.message: Saved. The popup will use $URL$ with the API key.

optionsSavedWithoutKey.message: Saved. The popup will use $URL$ without an API key.

optionsNoPermission.message: Permission to access that host wasn't granted, so the server has to allow extension requests itself (PhishNet 2.4.0 and newer do).

optionsKeyHint.message: Paste the API key that "phishnet serve" printed when it first started (stored in ~/.phishnet/api-key on the server), or make a new one with: phishnet serve --regenerate-key

optionsConnectedWithKey.message: Connected: PhishNet API is running at $URL$, and it accepts the API key.

optionsConnectedWithoutKey.message: Connected: PhishNet API is running at $URL$, and it accepts requests without a key.

optionsConnectedOldServer.message: Connected: PhishNet API is running at $URL$. It's older than 2.9.0, so it doesn't check API keys.
